adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:279 — .small-action-desc has no flex:1/min-width:0, so it shrink-wraps its content and long unbreakable text (URLs, usernames) can overflow the post stream width.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `.small-action` a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`), which turns `.small-action-desc` into a flex item. In this state, without an explicit `min-width: 0` (and/or `flex: 1`) on `.small-action-desc`, the default flex item `min-width: auto` can prevent it from shrinking below its intrinsic content width, so long unbreakable strings (e.g., URLs/usernames) can overflow the available post stream width. This risk is introduced/exposed by the new flex layout in `topic-post.scss`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:37 — Legacy display:-webkit-box/-moz-box fallbacks do not honor margin-left:auto push, so on old WebKit/Firefox the .panel is no longer right-aligned now that float:right was removed.

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.panel` loses `float: right` and is now positioned via flex (`.contents` gets `@include flexbox()` and `.panel` gets `margin-left: auto`). The new `flexbox()` mixin includes legacy `display: -webkit-box` / `display: -moz-box` fallbacks, and those older box models are not equivalent to modern flexbox behavior; relying on `margin-left: auto` for right-push can fail under those legacy displays. Thus the diff plausibly introduces a right-alignment regression in browsers that pick the legacy `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` modes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:18 — Flex items in .contents keep min-width:auto and no flex-shrink/overflow on .extra-info-wrapper, so a long topic title no longer wraps as with floats and can push .panel out of the header.

adjudication.rationale: In header.scss, `.contents` was changed from a non-flex container (with floated children) to a flex container via `@include flexbox()` and `@include align-items(center)`, and `.panel` is now positioned at the end using `margin-left: auto` plus `@include order(3)`. No flex sizing constraints (e.g., `min-width: 0`, `flex-shrink`, or overflow handling) were added for the other flex items (e.g., `.extra-info-wrapper`, which is now explicitly ordered in topic.scss with `@include order(2)`). With default flexbox behavior (`min-width: auto`), long text in a flex item commonly prevents shrinking/wrapping and can push the auto-margined `.panel` out, matching the reported regression risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:270 — .topic-avatar float:left is now ignored inside the flex .small-action and desc padding-left 4em was replaced by 1.5%, changing avatar/description spacing and removing the prior indent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `.small-action` a flex container (`@include flexbox();`), and changes `.small-action-desc` from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em;` to `padding: 0 1.5%;`, which clearly alters the avatar/description spacing and removes the previous left indent. If `.topic-avatar` is a direct child of `.small-action` (as implied by the nested selectors), its existing `float: left` would indeed no longer affect layout as a flex item, but this appears to be an intentional layout refactor rather than a provable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:116 — align-items mixin passes the modern value straight to -webkit-box-align/-ms-flex-align, which reject flex-start/flex-end (need start/end), so the mixin is wrong for those inputs; also -ms-align-items is not a real property.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `@mixin align-items($alignment)` in `mixins.scss` that directly assigns `$alignment` to legacy flexbox properties (`-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`) and also emits `-ms-align-items`, which is not a valid CSS property. Since `-webkit-box-align` expects legacy keywords (e.g., `start`/`end`) rather than modern `flex-start`/`flex-end`, the mixin is incorrect for those valid modern inputs, making this a real defect in the newly introduced mixin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:37 — margin-left:auto does not right-align children in legacy -webkit-box/-moz-box layout, so .panel loses its right alignment in fallback browsers after float:right was removed.

adjudication.rationale: In header.scss, `.contents` was changed from block layout to `@include flexbox()` (which outputs legacy `display: -webkit-box; display: -moz-box;` as well as modern flex), and `.panel` had `float: right;` removed and replaced with `margin-left: auto;` plus `@include order(3)`. The diff does not add any legacy box alignment property (e.g., `-webkit-box-pack: end`), and `margin-left:auto` is not a reliable right-alignment mechanism for the old `-webkit-box/-moz-box` model, so fallback browsers using those displays could lose the right-aligned panel behavior that `float:right` previously provided.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `.extra-info-wrapper` in `topic.scss` is (and was) a top-level selector; nothing indicates it was previously scoped to `.d-header .contents`, so the claim that `order`/`line-height` now “apply globally rather than scoped” is not supported by the diff. The removed `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` could affect alignment in some context, but the diff alone doesn’t verify a misalignment defect in the header specifically.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:121 — align-items mixin emits nonexistent `-ms-align-items` property (dead output; IE10 uses only -ms-flex-align).
matched_golden_ids: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the mixin outputs `-ms-align-items`, which is a nonexistent legacy property, and notes that IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align` instead—matching the golden issue that `-ms-align-items` never existed and the correct property is `-ms-flex-align`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:117 — align-items mixin passes raw flexbox values to legacy -webkit-box-align/-ms-flex-align, which expect start/end, so flex-start/flex-end calls silently break.

adjudication.rationale: The new `@mixin align-items($alignment)` (mixins.scss) forwards `$alignment` directly to legacy properties `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those legacy syntaxes expect keywords like `start`/`end` (not `flex-start`/`flex-end`), so invoking `@include align-items(flex-start)` or `flex-end` would emit invalid legacy declarations and break alignment in older flexbox implementations. This mismatch is evident from the mixin’s implementation in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:125 — order mixin maps to -webkit-box-ordinal-group 1:1 though that property is 1-based and rejects 0/negatives, so the abstraction is wrong for legacy browsers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an `@mixin order($val)` that maps `$val` directly to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`. That legacy property is 1-based (unlike modern `order`, which is 0-based and allows negatives), so a direct 1:1 mapping can yield incorrect/invalid behavior in older WebKit if callers pass 0 or negative values. In this diff it’s only used with positive values (`order(2)`, `order(3)`), so no concrete break is shown here, but the mixin abstraction is still flawed for legacy-browser compatibility.
